1.0 INTRODUCTION:

1.1 To ensure the policies regarding Therapeutic diet (Poshana Karma).

2.0 SCOPE:

2.1 Hospital Management

2.2 Health Care Providers

2.3 Patients

2.4 Government agencies

3.0 RESPONSIBILITY:

3.1 Doctors

3.2 Dietician

3.3 Nursing staff

4.0 ABBREVIATIONS:

4.1 COP-Care of Patient

5.0 DEFINITION: Nil

6.0 REFERENCE:

6.1 NABH : Accreditation Standards For Ayurveda Hospitals 2nd Edition April 2016.

7.0 OBJECTIVE ELEMENTS

7.1. Documented policies and procedures guide implementation of therapeutic diet (Poshana karma) after assessment and reassessment of patient needs.

7.2. Patients receive food according to their clinical needs.

7.3. There is a written order for the Pathyahara.

7.4. When families provide food, they are educated about the patient’s Pathya and apathya.

7.5. Food is prepared, handled, stored and distributed in a safe manner.

8. 0 PROCESSES

8.1 Dietician/doctor will assess the prepared food and ensure that the patient receives food as per the diet order. Assessment will be done by a doctor for all patients found at risk during screening. [Ref Manual of therapeutic diet]

8.1.2 The treating Doctor does the assessment of the patient and advises food accordingly as per the need of the patient.

8.1.3 Diet plan has to be prepared by dietician/doctor it should be given as per diseased nature and if any changes in planning of therapeutic diet it should be verified by treating doctor. This will take in a soft copy and this will attach in a uniform location in the medical record.

8.2 Patients receive food according to their clinical needs.

8.3 There is written order in care plan

8.4 Families providing food have to be guided by a treating doctor regarding Pathya and apathya.

8.5 The dietary services are outsourced. All the activities fall in a sequence. Food is prepared, handled, stored and distributed in a safe manner. The hospital ensures that hygienic conditions are followed all throughout. Other indicative points are:

i. Dedicated food storage/refrigeration areas exist to ensure food preservation;

ii. Food storage areas/refrigerators are maintained appropriately;

iii. All food products are stored off the floor;

iv. Cleaning supplies stored in a separate location away from food;

v. Separate dedicated food preparation areas exist;

vi. Measures are in place to ensure that flies/insects/contaminating vectors do not come in contact with prepared/stored food;

Vii. Food distribution to patients occurs where possible in temperature appropriate food tiffins
